answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously, adding one per fatigue on that card and one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the member to Pensioners, flips the card to Vacant Offices, and returns its fatigue to supply.

Players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to most total windows (including new prizes), then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. There is no immediate replacement; when the display empties, remaining players skip selection. Discard remaining display cards and refill three even if nobody took one. Return unused Pensioners to their supplies.

Each player takes one chosen family action and puts their opportunity marker on it. If the marker was already on that action at phase start, the action can be taken twice. Only the latest passed extra-action law may be used; its extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn, so the doubled action places three writers total.

After family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one, repeating while both remain. If there is no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving order. The share purchase price was paid to the bank; seeking a share does not put family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—New Company shares; Seek Share row

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on their card backs. To hire your own family member, obtain verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces a pure majority of current shares (more than half); any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate supported by that many shares wins. If no candidate gets enough support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself; no Nepotism consent applies. The winner's Company share moves to the Chairman slot and remains a share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

Commit resources/cash, gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll; use the lowest die. A 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office limits allow, and 5–6 is catastrophic: no more office actions, return the officeholder to supply, discard fatigue, and flip the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success (for example, trade with no ship or deploy without dice to trigger possible officer losses).

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, gaining £5 Balance for each. Each further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (counting the Chairman), and Debt may never pass the track end. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved within those limits; cash already in office treasuries stays there.

Shipping must spend treasury cash until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Acquired ships go to any sea zone, including China once that office exists; extra ships last only until Refresh.

Declare regions including the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. After success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions: first writer goes to home port and each later order must be adjacent to one already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President may not fill another Presidency's home region, even if its office is vacant. Increase Balance by printed order values; the President earns £1 per order and writer owners £1 per placed writer. At most one successful Trade per President per turn; failure can be retried if affordable, while catastrophe removes the President.

A Commander may target its Presidency's home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for Deploy to have an effect. Exhausted officers and regiments each provide one die; local alliances provide their printed dice. Subtract target tower strength plus its whole empire's strength (Company defense is zero). After every attempt, each player with officers exhausted in it rolls one die per officer; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.

On success, loot equals £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot-token modifier, with at least one plus the number of surviving used officers. Distribute proceeds in cycles: £1 Commander share plus £1 per its used surviving officer; clockwise £1 per other player's used surviving officer; then £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece, repeating until cash is gone. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Remove tower/dome, open orders and clear unrest; if newly Company-controlled, place its control token and Governor overlay and add the office card to vacancies. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half its family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.

The Governor rolls its printed dice pool with no penalty, reducing the pool by one after each result. Success pays £1, plus £1 if the previous roll failed, and allows Build, Commission, or Tax. Each unsuccessful check adds unrest. Tax adds £2 to Balance or the President's treasury; each Tax after the first that turn adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or suffering catastrophe (which follows normal office removal).

Company expenses are £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until the track end; loans continue even at maximum Debt, and newly added Debt does not add current-turn expense. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if short. The Chairman may then pay affordable dividends; if dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.

An attack on a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary first, then in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order the Commanders resolve attacks in their Presidencies. For the primary, use normal attack strength plus local unrest; each secondary uses only that region's unrest. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling that attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, the region is lost; otherwise clear all unrest there and the Commander takes one trophy. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs chooses a substitute, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; the substitute gains/loses no trophies.

The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time and selects one (a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing), chooses the matching policy direction, and sets the vote marker to printed starting support. Voting adjusts support. At -1 or less, the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma's failure text, the Opposition Leader takes the PM dial, the new PM moves the proposed policy one space either way and resolves that adjacent policy. At zero or more, the law passes: keep it among passed laws, PM takes a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then immediate law effects. Restore vote cards afterward. If a law causes failure, finish the vote before final scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Passing lowers Debt by one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives the PM a passed-law token, and activates firms. Failing increases Company share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token (maximum ±3). It has no policy; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against. 1813 begins deregulated.

To form a firm, a player not already managing one returns an eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to invested; flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set value to the leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into London treasury. With manager consent, further eligible Company shares or workshops create firm shares and add £5 from bank to London. At most ten shares; further investments still add £5 but no shares. Chairman shares cannot be used; no Company shares may be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created this turn cannot be used. Invested workshops never return to uninvested and lose their bonus and Company-failure VP.

The manager secretly selects a sea zone/home port and London cash bid, requiring a ship, or selects Hobnob with no bid. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before actions, matching firms reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice; a successful President's Trade gets the same calculation from Presidency ships. Following the President's success, orders are filled by lowest initiative, President first on ties. If President is vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governor chances, with Chairman breaking initiative ties. Each firm fills up to ships+1 open orders, starting at home port and tracing its own filled route; it may fill an order only once, but may refill orders filled by others this turn. Previously filled orders yield half listed revenue rounded down. Add revenue to India treasury and advance firm value one space per full £6 added that turn.

At Revenue start, before the Company, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm value, using either or both treasuries. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India treasury: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; a shareholder may forgo payments on shares with manager consent. Record actual total cash paid out; active non-Hobnob firms with no payout record zero, while Hobnob retains its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. If unable to pay expenses, the firm dissolves unless rescued through emergency investments or a merger with one other firm. On dissolution shares go to Debtor's Prison (each costs 1 VP), ships return to shipyards, charter returns to family side, and workshops remain invested.
